name: (DEP) Pod has CPU contention due to long wait for I/O events
description: Pod is experiencing high I/O wait. I/O wait represents the amount of time that a Pod is waiting for completion of I/O events. Disk and network I/O operations are common causes of I/O wait because they are the slowest operations in the system. High I/O wait can be due to a poorly performing storage device on which the Pod resides. A device in the virtual machine configuration that stops functioning or responding can also trigger high I/O wait. These devices can include but are not limited to serial pass-through, parallel pass-through and USB devices. For example, high I/O wait can occur when an ISO file that is left mounted in the Pod is accidentally deleted or moved to an alternate location

The condition can also occur if the available resources are not usable by a Pod because of fragmentation, or the Pod is unable to run on hosts that have available capacity. description: A host is reported as network-partitioned if both the following conditions are met: - The vSphere HA master host to which vCenter Server is connected is unable to communicate with the host by using the management network, but is able to communicate with that host by using the heartbeat datastores that have been selected for it. - The host is not isolated. A network partition can occur for a number of reasons including incorrect VLAN tagging, the failure of a physical NIC or switch, configuring a cluster with some hosts that use only IPv4 and others that use only IPv6, or the management networks for some hosts were moved to a different virtual switch without first putting the host into maintenance mode. While the virtual machines running on the host continue to be monitored by the master hosts that are responsible for them, vSphere HA's ability to restart the virtual machines after a failure is affected. Further, each master host has access to a subset of the hosts, so less failover capacity is available to each host.

A host is network isolated if both of the following conditions are met: - Isolation addresses are configured and the host is unable to ping the addresses. - The vSphere HA agent on the host cannot access any of the agents that are running on the other cluster hosts. When a host is network-isolated, it continues to monitor the virtual machines that remain powered-on. Host network isolation affects how vSphere HA restarts virtual machines after a failure. vSphere HA powers off or shuts down a virtual machine only if the agent on the host determines that a master host is responsible for the virtual machine.
